summary: We developed a theory-concept tool that measures turbidity data in a river (River Pra) in Ghana to produce enough data to be able to compare with turbidity data pulled from NASA's HLSS30 and HLSL30.
details: There is a tool that in theory will measure turbidity changes in River Pra, Ghana, and will have its data plotted on a graph. In addition, turbidity data from that point where the tool theoretically will be placed is also pulled from NASA's HLSS30 and HLSL30 to also plot a graph to ascertain whether recent changes in turbidity levels are due to storms in the rainy seasons or other factors like illegal mining. The intended impact is to raise awareness about the illegal mining situation and how it affects rivers in Ghana. The tools used were Blender, VS CODE, PowerPoint, Claude AI, Ellipsus, and Discord for communication. It is creative because it explores an angle in detecting effects of illegal mining in rivers by turbidity levels. The factors we considered were: whether to use solar panels or battery for the power source of the tool, what parts of the River Pra to base the tool in, what to show for the tool since it was a theoretical concept with no prototype,and by what means to present data.
